architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with substantial thermal-hold drift in at least one local formulation.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 formulation showed a measured 15-60 min relative viscosity change of 0.5154 (51.54%) at 120 C, compared with 0.0951 (9.51%) for E1 over the same window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data provide only two original thermal-hold formulations, each with four points over 15-90 min, and the reported comparison is mainly the 15-60 min endpoint change. This leaves the shape and reproducibility of the time-dependent trajectory under modified chemistry poorly resolved, whereas temperature response has six-point 80-130 C sweeps across multiple runs and realized viscosity level has measured repeat-spread summaries, despite substantial state uncertainty.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate and a suitable matched reference at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 without extrapolation.
Use at least two independent preparation repeats and record the full process history so drift can be distinguished from realization-state variation.
Keep the reactive mass fraction and measurement window matched across the comparison, while explicitly identifying whether the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes are active.
Compare the observed drift with the pre-result linear-dilution prediction and the registered superlinear-suppression and tackifier-required criteria.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and a matched 120 C residence window, does modifier chemistry reduce viscosity drift substantially below the linear reactive-core dilution prediction, and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is non-zero rather than with an acrylic-like modifier alone? The outcome separates H-CORE from H-RESIN and tests H-DUAL.

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL: a low-drift outcome supports both and does not distinguish superlinear resin suppression from tackifier-required specialization.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below half the linear-dilution prediction, approximately 3.80% for reactive mass fraction 0.80, the result supports H-RESIN and is consistent with H-DUAL because the minor tackifier-like axis is active; it rejects H-CORE as the sole explanation.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains at or above the linear-dilution prediction, approximately 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the proposed superlinear suppression is not observed. H-DUAL is also falsified for this nonzero-tackifier composition, while H-CORE is supported if the result agrees with the prediction within the stated 2 percentage-point resolution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between approximately 3.80% and 7.61% indicates partial suppression but does not meet the registered H-RESIN acceptance rule or decisively establish H-DUAL; it would require a follow-up comparison with an acrylic-only composition or a different tackifier loading.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only composition directly tests H-CORE versus H-RESIN and can falsify H-DUAL if drift is low, but a near-linear result leaves H-CORE and H-DUAL observationally confounded.

The 5% minor-tackifier-only composition is within the supported minor-resin region and tests tackifier involvement, but it provides less direct evidence for the combined resin-suppression intervention and cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL when drift is low.
The 10% minor-tackifier-only composition is a larger single-axis perturbation and has the same fundamental limitation of not distinguishing H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41 uses 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, both inside externally supported intervention regions, while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions and giving a reactive mass fraction of 0.80. The direct 120 C matched-window hold measures the declared least-resolved failure coordinate without model fitting or extrapolation. Its linear reference is 9.51% × 0.80 = 7.61%, while the registered superlinear criterion is below 3.80%. A dual-axis card therefore gives the strongest single-experiment separation of reactive-core behavior from both resin suppression and tackifier-required behavior, despite not separating H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from the confounded dual-axis S1C41 hold to the listed acrylic-only S1C39 hold to obtain the missing single-axis contrast. The result should be interpreted together with a matched minor-tackifier-only and dual-axis comparison before claiming H-DUAL.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Deterministic VOI scores, tied top experiment IDs, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary are withheld, so membership in a deterministic top set cannot be established. The proposal is therefore not supported as a documented deterministic-top-set choice.
residual_decision_risk: S1C39 alone cannot complete the recommended factorial comparison or establish tackifier necessity.
Only two preparation repeats are specified despite substantial E2 realization-state variability at 120 C.
No prespecified repeat-level aggregation or boundary-classification rule is supplied.
Acrylic-only results may remain insufficient to distinguish general resin effects from acrylic-specific effects without the reactive-core and dual-axis controls.
The absence of VOI scores and perturbation boundaries prevents assessment of score-margin robustness.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is decisive for the stated hypothesis-discrimination objective: S1C41 activates both modifier axes, so even a low SI_15_60 cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish that the minor tackifier is required. A matched single-axis contrast is therefore needed before attributing suppression to modifier specialization. S1C39::M-HOLD-120 supplies the listed acrylic-only contrast, although a complete factorial comparison including reactive-core control, acrylic-only, minor-tackifier-only, and dual-axis compositions would be preferable.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight perturbation results are supplied because the VOI scoring layer is withheld. Consequently, no defensible weight scaling or recommendation_flip_boundary can be identified; the decision must rest on the supplied scientific evidence rather than inferred score stability.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The H-RESIN falsification criterion is operationally measurable because SI_15_60 is read directly from viscosity at 15 and 60 minutes, without fitting or extrapolation. The predicted linear value is 7.61%, the acceptance threshold is 3.80%, and their 3.81 percentage-point separation exceeds the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. Nevertheless, only two repeats and the documented E2 state variability make classification near the boundary practically fragile unless a prespecified repeat-level decision rule is added.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low drift near or below 3.80% would support combined-modifier performance and reject a pure linear-dilution explanation, but would not support the stronger attribution that tackifier activity is necessary or that acrylic addition alone would remain near the linear prediction.
objections.objection: The proposed S1C41 composition contains both 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, so one low SI_15_60 result cannot establish the registered H-DUAL claim that the minor tackifier is required. It is compatible with either H-RESIN or H-DUAL. The proposer admits H-RESIN versus H-DUAL is unseparated in hypotheses_not_separated, but the hypotheses_separated field and reasoning still claim that the experiment tests H-DUAL as a specialization.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could justify only a performance statement for the combined 15%/5% intervention relative to the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction; claims about modifier-axis specialization or mechanism would remain unsupported.
objections.objection: The intervention changes both registered modifier axes simultaneously: acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total is 15% and minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total is 5%. Therefore any SI_15_60 suppression cannot be attributed to the acrylic axis, the tackifier axis, or their interaction. The matched reactive_mass_fraction of 0.80 removes the first-order mass-dilution difference used in the H-CORE calculation, but it does not remove the two-axis composition confounding.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may reject H-CORE or fail to meet H-RESIN's threshold, but it cannot claim that the minor tackifier is the required axis.
objections.objection: The registered H-DUAL supported_if condition requires low drift only for compositions with non-zero minor tackifier fraction. S1C41 measures only one non-zero-tackifier composition and does not include the listed acrylic-only alternative S1C39. Thus it cannot distinguish 'tackifier required' from 'any resin modification suppresses drift,' even though the outcome_interpretation says a low result is consistent with H-DUAL.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result close to the 7.61% boundary could be labeled H-RESIN-falsifying without demonstrating that the observed difference is chemistry rather than preparation-state variation.
objections.objection: The numerical falsification boundary is attainable in principle: the protocol directly measures SI_15_60 and compares 7.61% with the 3.80% H-RESIN threshold, a separation of about 3.81 percentage points that exceeds the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. However, the protocol specifies only two independent preparation repeats, while the supplied E2 evidence shows a 120 C realization max/min viscosity ratio of 3.57 and CV of 0.5848. No drift-specific repeatability or prespecified aggregation rule is supplied to show that a single composition-level SI estimate can reliably classify results close to 7.61%.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single dual-axis S1C41 hold with a matched factorial comparison at reactive mass fraction 0.80: reactive-core control, acrylic-only composition, minor-tackifier-only composition, and the 15% acrylic plus 5% tackifier composition, each with at least two independent preparations and the same 15-60 minute SI_15_60 endpoint. This would test the tackifier-required contrast directly while retaining the H-CORE versus H-RESIN comparison.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The S1C41 intervention activates both modifier axes at once, so the primary SI_15_60 result cannot identify which axis causes suppression; in particular, a low result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish that the minor tackifier is required.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
